None of the snippets directly tests or reports this inverse-rate-versus-ultimate-length relationship. Most snippets simply report VBGF parameter estimates for various fish/invertebrate species (single food/field conditions) or discuss optimal-allocation interpretations of growth curves, which are topically adjacent but bear no quantitative weight on the claim. Snippet 18 reports that VB-modelled convergence rates were unrealistic for Daphnia under variable food, weakly cutting against the model's adequacy. Overall the corpus offers no clear, direct evidence for or against the fact, so support is weak and the direction is essentially neutral/insufficient.

snippets.title: Do Bertalanffy's growth curves result from optimal resource allocation?
snippets.label: neutral
snippets.text: Bertalanffy's equation is commonly used to model indeterminate growth. Bertalanffy claimed that this growth pattern results from growth potential decreasing with age. An alternative approach provided by life history theory predicts that indeterminate growth is optimal for organisms in a seasonal environment and results not from decreasing growth potential but from allocating increasingly less energy with age into growth, and more into reproduction.

snippets.label: neutral
snippets.text: Several phenomenological descriptions, such as the von Bertalanffy growth model, have been widely used to describe size-at-age and individual growth across a diverse range of organisms. However, for modelling life histories, as opposed to just growth, biologically and mechanistically meaningful growth models, based on allocation decisions, have become increasingly important.
